SK1122 A nearby anonymous type has the same members in another order

Two anonymous object creations in one member with the same member names and types but a different order, which makes them two runtime types.

CategoryModernization
Default severityhint
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, review it
Language version floor—
Since2.0
ReSharperSimilarAnonymousTypeNearby (resharper_similar_anonymous_type_nearby_highlighting)

Why

Anonymous types unify on the ordered list of member names and types, so a pair that differs only in order is a pair of types. Nothing at the point of use says so: both are var, both print the same members, and the cost appears later as a dictionary with two key types, a Distinct that removes nothing, a Union that concatenates, and an assignment that does not compile for a reason the error message states in terms of two generated names.

Example

Instead of:

var head = new { Id = id, Name = name };
var tail = new { Name = name, Id = id };

Write:

var head = new { Id = id, Name = name };
var tail = new { Id = id, Name = name };

When it does not fire

⚠ The premise was established by compiling and running it, and half of what the inspection's name suggests is a no-op the compiler already performs. Two anonymous object creations with the same member names, the same member types and the same order are already one type — the same Type instance, across methods, within an assembly — so there is nothing to reuse there and the rule is silent. ⚠ Order is what creates a second type: new { X = 1, Y = "s" } compiles to <>f__AnonymousType0 and new { Y = "s", X = 1 } to <>f__AnonymousType1, and the two are distinct at run time. A member name or a member type that differs is a genuinely different shape and is not reported — there is no edit that makes those one type. ⚠ Reordering is only free where the initializers are. The edit moves the initializer expressions past one another, so it changes the order in which they are evaluated; the rule matches only a chain of plain names, for which that is unobservable, and declines an initializer holding a call, an await or an element access. ⚠ `fixIsSafe: false` even so, because the runtime type is what the fix changes — that is the point — and the member order is visible through ToString() and through anything that serialises the object. ⚠ The two must be in the same member. Anonymous types unify across a whole assembly, so a wider search would report a pair whose halves cannot be read side by side, which is the "nearby" in the inspection's own name. ⚠ A creation in a different assembly is a different type whatever its shape, confirmed in the same probe, and is out of reach of any edit. ⚠ The earliest matching creation in the member is the one the fix reorders towards, so the pair and the edit are the same whichever half is analysed. A creation with fewer than two members cannot be reordered and is not considered. A comment or a preprocessor directive inside the replaced span withdraws the finding. Generated code is excluded.
